$comment: Everyday events (domain/events/spec.md §5.22, EVT-115 to EVT-128; feedback 152). Small choices about the realm's own people and stores, drawn from what the game already holds: its officials, lords, ruler and heir, and food stores, plague reaching a province of the player's (EVT-130: not drawn; plague fires it), and the death of one of the player's officials, lords, generals or admirals (EVT-122, EVT-123, EVT-132: not drawn; the death of people fires it). Each realm draws one every `months_between` months (a range), never while the player has an event waiting; the player's realm never draws the same event again within `rest_years` (EVT-134). `where` limits an event to realms in those regions or wider regions (exploration-regions.json), `from` and `to` to those years (EVT-133). `weight` is how often an event is drawn among the ones that can happen; `needs` names what it is about. Options list their effects in the engine's small vocabulary (gold, loyalty, official, lands, heir, heir_risk, food_back, new_lord, quarantine, care, command, home; and for an event about a province, EVT-135: food in months of eating, people and recruits as a share, light_tax in years); `ai` weights the AI's pick; `needs` on an option hides it when the realm lacks what it asks (`lord2`: a second lord; `leaderless`: the dead commander's men or ships still without a leader). `{words}` in braces are filled with the names of who and where. Every number is a placeholder for balance.

official_dies.title: Death of {dead}
official_dies.text: {dead}, your {type} at {province}, has died after {years} years in the post. The seat stands empty, and his clerks wait to hear who will take it.

lord_dies.title: Death of {dead}
lord_dies.text: {dead} of the house of {house} has died. His heir {son} has taken his lands ({lands}) and asks you to confirm him in them.

options.name: Ask a fee for his lands
Take his lands for the crown

general_dies.title: Death of {dead}
general_dies.text: {dead}, your general, has died at {province}. Without him his men take no orders and make for crown land, to stand there as a garrison. His second in command, {second}, asks to lead them in his place.

admiral_dies.title: Death of {dead}
admiral_dies.text: {dead}, your admiral, has died at {province}. Without him his ships take no orders and make for the nearest port of yours. His flag captain, {second}, asks to keep the fleet at sea under his own flag.

lord_slighted.title: {lord} feels slighted
lord_slighted.text: {lord} of the house of {house} was seated below a lesser man at your table, and talks against you in his hall.

options.name: Give him an office at court

lord_praises.title: {lord} speaks well of you
lord_praises.text: {lord} of the house of {house} has been heard praising your rule in his hall. A word from you now could win him over.

lords_quarrel.title: {lord} and {lord2} quarrel
lords_quarrel.text: {lord} and {lord2} both claim a mill and its meadows on the edge of their lands, and each asks you to judge for him.

options.name: Fine them both and keep the mill

lord_hurt.title: {lord} is hurt
lord_hurt.text: {lord} of the house of {house} fell from his horse while hunting and lies in his hall with a broken leg.

child_born.title: A child is born
child_born.text: A {child} is born to {ruler}, and named {childName}. The bells ring in every town of the realm.

heir_ill.title: {heir} falls ill
heir_ill.text: Your heir {heir}, aged {heirAge}, is burning with fever. The court physicians shake their heads.

grain_rots.title: Grain rots at {province}
grain_rots.text: Damp has got into the granaries at {province}. The keepers have thrown out {loss} months of grain.

granary_fire.title: Fire in the granary at {province}
granary_fire.text: A fire in the night has burned half of {province}'s granary: {loss} months of grain are lost.

plague_reaches.title: Plague at {province}
plague_reaches.text: Men are falling sick at {province}: fever, black swellings, death in three days. The townsfolk die first. What will you do?

options.name: Send physicians and burn the sick houses

rats.title: Rats in the stores at {province}
rats.text: Rats have overrun the stores at {province} and spoiled {loss} months of grain.

good_harvest.title: A rich harvest at {province}
good_harvest.text: The barns at {province} are full to the rafters, and the reeves say they have not seen such a year in living memory.

hail.title: Hail at {province}
hail.text: A storm of hail has flattened the standing corn at {province}. The villagers ask how they are to pay this year's tax.

options.name: Lighten their tax for a year

bandits.title: Bandits near {province}
bandits.text: A band of outlaws holds the woods on the road to {province}. Carters go armed, and some no longer go at all.

options.name: Send men to hunt them down

bridge_falls.title: The bridge at {province} falls
bridge_falls.text: Spring floods have carried away the old bridge at {province}. Traders now wait days for the ferry.

town_fire.title: Fire in {province}
town_fire.text: A fire that began in a baker's oven has burned a whole quarter of the town of {province}.

options.name: Rebuild in stone, at your cost

flood.title: The river floods at {province}
flood.text: The river has burst its banks at {province}, drowning fields and filling cellars with mud.

options.name: Wait for the waters to fall

scholar.title: A scholar comes to court
scholar.text: A learned man, driven from his own land, asks leave to teach at {province} under your protection.

market_charter.title: {lord} asks for a market
market_charter.text: {lord} of the house of {house} asks your leave to hold a weekly market at {province}, and to take its tolls.

options.name: Hold the market for the crown

walls_without_leave.title: {lord} raises walls
walls_without_leave.text: {lord} of the house of {house} is building walls and towers at {province} without asking your leave.

skimming_official.title: Your official at {province} is skimming
skimming_official.text: Merchants complain that {official}, your {type} at {province}, keeps back part of the tolls for himself.

veterans.title: Old soldiers at {province}
veterans.text: Old soldiers with nowhere to go have gathered at {province}, asking for land to farm.

wolves.title: Wolves at {province}
wolves.text: A hard winter has driven wolves down from the hills at {province}. They take sheep, and a shepherd boy is missing.

options.name: Pay a bounty on every pelt
Let the shepherds deal with it

tutor.title: A tutor for {heir}
tutor.text: Your heir {heir}, aged {heirAge}, is old enough for lessons. Who shall teach the child?

options.name: Hire the most learned man you can find

omen.title: A comet over {province}
omen.text: A star with a burning tail hangs over {province} night after night. The people whisper that it foretells the death of kings.

silver_found.title: Silver at {province}
silver_found.text: A shepherd at {province} has found a seam of silver ore in a gully. Miners are already gathering.

options.name: Let the miners dig as they will

pilgrims.title: Pilgrims at {province}
pilgrims.text: Word of a holy relic at {province} has spread, and pilgrims crowd the roads. The innkeepers grow rich.

tournament.title: A tournament
tournament.text: {lord} and the young men of your lords' houses beg you to hold a tournament, with jousting and a feast.

options.name: There are better uses for gold

guilds_quarrel.title: Guilds quarrel at {province}
guilds_quarrel.text: The weavers' and dyers' guilds of {province} have come to blows over who may sell cloth in the market.

printer.title: A printer at {province}
printer.text: A printer with a press of movable letters asks leave to set up shop at {province}. The scribes say it is the devil's work.

witch_trials.title: Accusations at {province}
witch_trials.text: After a bad harvest, the people of {province} accuse an old widow of witchcraft, and name others besides.

enclosure.title: {lord} fences the commons
enclosure.text: {lord} is fencing the common fields at {province} for his sheep. The villagers who grazed them there have nowhere to go.

coffee_house.title: Coffee houses at {province}
coffee_house.text: Coffee houses have sprung up all over {province}. Men sit in them for hours, talking of trade and of your government.

railway.title: A railway through {province}
railway.text: Surveyors ask leave to lay a railway line through {province}, and a grant to help pay for it.

options.name: Let the company pay its own way

strike.title: A strike at {province}
strike.text: The mill hands of {province} have walked out, asking for shorter hours and higher pay.

options.name: Press the owners to give way

cholera.title: Cholera at {province}
cholera.text: Cholera has broken out in the poor streets of {province}. Doctors blame the bad air; one says it is the water.

options.name: Burn tar against the bad air

newspaper.title: A newspaper attacks your ministers
newspaper.text: A newspaper at {province} prints, week after week, that your ministers are fools and thieves. It sells very well.

caravan_raided.title: A caravan raided near {province}
caravan_raided.text: Raiders fell on a caravan a day's ride from {province}, and the merchants want to know what you will do.

options.name: Pay the tribes to keep the peace

qanat.title: The water channels at {province} fail
qanat.text: The underground channels that bring water to the fields of {province} have caved in, and the wells are falling.

locusts.title: Locusts at {province}
locusts.text: A cloud of locusts darkened the sky over {province} for a day. When it lifted, {loss} months of grain were gone from the fields and stores.

endowment.title: An endowment at {province}
endowment.text: A rich merchant of {province} wishes to leave his shops to a school and a fountain for ever, free of tax.

gold_traders.title: Gold traders at {province}
gold_traders.text: Traders from the north have come to {province} with salt and cloth, seeking gold dust.

cattle_raid.title: Cattle raided at {province}
cattle_raid.text: Raiders from beyond the border have driven off the herds of {province}. The young men want to go after them.

options.name: Give the herders cattle of your own

rains_late.title: The rains are late at {province}
rains_late.text: The rains have not come to {province}, and the sown fields are turning to dust. The priests ask for offerings.

monsoon_fails.title: The monsoon fails at {province}
monsoon_fails.text: The monsoon has failed at {province}. The rice withers in dry paddies, and {loss} months of grain are already eaten.

temple_festival.title: A festival at {province}
temple_festival.text: The great temple festival at {province} draws crowds from far away. The priests ask the crown to pay for the procession.

revenue_survey.title: A survey of {province}
revenue_survey.text: Your revenue clerks say the land registers of {province} are a generation out of date, and much land pays nothing.

river_dykes.title: The dykes at {province} weaken
river_dykes.text: The river officials report that the dykes at {province} are rotten, and the next flood may break through.

options.name: Call out labour to repair them

exam_scandal.title: Cheating at the examinations
exam_scandal.text: Candidates at {province} were found with answers sewn into their sleeves, and your {type}, {official}, is said to have sold the questions.

pirates.title: Pirates off {province}
pirates.text: Pirates have burned fishing boats off {province} and carried away the crews to sell.

tea_master.title: A tea master at {province}
tea_master.text: A famous master of tea and poetry has come to {province}. Your lords would give much to sit at his gatherings.

spice_merchants.title: Spice ships at {province}
spice_merchants.text: Ships heavy with pepper and cloves have put in at {province}, and their captains ask what dues they must pay.

options.name: Light dues, to bring more ships

ball_game.title: The great ball game
ball_game.text: {lord} challenges your court's team to the ball game, with feathers, jade and honour wagered on it.

maize_blight.title: Blight in the maize at {province}
maize_blight.text: A blight has blackened the maize at {province}, and {loss} months of grain have rotted on the cob.

voyagers.title: Voyagers at {province}
voyagers.text: Great canoes have come in to {province} from islands far away, bringing new plants and stories.

horse_fair.title: A horse fair at {province}
horse_fair.text: Herders from the steppe have brought thousands of horses to sell at {province}.

hard_winter.title: A hard winter at {province}
hard_winter.text: Ice and deep snow have lain on {province} since autumn. Animals die in the byres, and the fodder is nearly gone.

fur_tribute.title: Furs from {province}
fur_tribute.text: Trappers bring sable and fox to {province}, more than any year before. The merchants want to buy the whole lot.

options.name: Take the best for the crown
